name: Window Control
description:
Control windows from a script, a rules file or the keyboard, on Wayland and X11.

* Scripts: a D-Bus interface lists the open windows with ID, title, WM class, PID, workspace, monitor and geometry. It can activate, move, resize, minimize, maximize, fullscreen, set above, set sticky or close a window. This does on Wayland what wmctrl does on X11.
* Rules: ~/.config/gnome-window-control/rules.json places new windows automatically. The extension creates that directory, reads the file and never writes it. Without the file no window is placed.
* Keyboard: Super+Ctrl and a numpad key tile the focused window on a 4x2 grid. Every shortcut is a GSettings key that you can rebind or unbind.

The extension has no preferences window and adds nothing to the panel. It registers the D-Bus object /org/gnome/Shell/Extensions/WindowControl on the org.gnome.Shell bus name. When you disable the extension, the D-Bus object, the shortcuts and the automatic placement stop; rules.json stays.

IMPORTANT: the interface has no access control. Any application in your session can call it to read window titles and to control your windows. This is necessary for the intended use from shell scripts. Do not enable the extension if that is not acceptable to you.

The command-line client wctl and the full documentation are on the project page. wctl is not part of this extension and is not installed with it.
